scope: Exact preparation of independent Linux replacement children; production single replacement uses the same group preparation and pre-promotion cancellation boundary
contracts: Every exact source/target/private-root request is selected before one atomic group admission; every child is bound before any executable child is returned
Preparation uses captured physical paths and records source/original versions and parent identity, sharing complete OperationRecord validation and manifest-size preflight with promotion

A binding/cancellation/validation error explicitly attempts retirement of every admitted child, preserving primary errors and bounded cleanup detail; preparation creates no durable catalog or user-file effects
Cancellation already observed at executor entry retires the child before promotion without durable recovery work
Two independent children execute exact destinations and restore independent originals; a completed sibling retains a usable native inverse when a later child is cancelled or its source changes
Alias retargeting after preparation never redirects execution; changed target identity before binding is rejected without touching either object

independent_review.result: ACCEPTED for bounded preparation and singleton production scope; source/tests and final Rust log reviewed independently
confirmed: Whole group admitted before executable children escape
Explicit cleanup attempts across failed sibling retirement
Exact paths/versions survive alias and source changes
Pre-promotion cancellation and independent inverse receipt
qualifications: Native versions are captured sequentially after admission, not an atomic filesystem snapshot
Internal admission failure can leave unindexed owner locks for later reclamation
Dropping or panicking with prepared children still relies on abandoned-owner reclamation
Pre-catalog promotion failure is conservatively uncertain
No mixed transfer or grouped IPC/history acceptance

limitations: Independent replacements only: mixed ordinary copies, ordered overlapping targets, same-name policy, native batch IPC and paste/drop migration remain open
No partial-result ledger that survives later worker panic, no one-job cancellation/progress lifecycle, and no grouped forward history are introduced
Same-object version changes after preparation are checked during execution; external writers, timestamp restoration, nested edits and inode reuse retain existing observation limits
Preparation retirement failures are reported; damaged storage may require later reconciliation
Cancellation can race the pre-promotion check and then require durable recovery; publication must finish after displacement
No Windows/macOS qualification, artifact retirement, whole-review completion, publication, or measured half-bounce startup claim
